en: Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 8.27. Ganthaniyaduka (The Couple of Factors Concerning What is to be Grasped)
Dependent on a state that is not subject to bondage, a state that is not subject to bondage arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not subject to bondage, a state that is subject to bondage arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not subject to bondage, states both not subject to bondage and subject to bondage arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not to be tied by knots (*na-āganthaniya*), a state that is not to be tied by knots arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is both [to be tied by knots] and not to be tied by knots, a state that is not to be tied by knots arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are five;
under object-condition there are two ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there are five. (In all cases, there are five.)
